subject.title: feat: version field in health response + POST /admin/update endpoint

question: Should OpenClaw expose host package updates over HTTP for trusted fleet tooling, and if yes should that be a dedicated `/admin/update` route or an opt-in `admin-http-rpc` allowlist expansion for `update.run` with target-version support?
rationale: The remaining work changes a host-level control-plane boundary, duplicates or extends existing update surfaces, and may allow remote package mutation by any Gateway operator-token holder; automation cannot choose that security/product contract safely.

options.title: Extend existing admin HTTP RPC after review
options.body: Expose `update.run` through the existing disabled-by-default `admin-http-rpc` plugin only after maintainers approve the method, params, docs, private-ingress guidance, and tests.

options.title: Add a dedicated endpoint
options.body: Create `/admin/update` as a separate core HTTP route with its own schema and docs, accepting the extra surface area and duplication risk.

options.title: Do not expose HTTP updates
options.body: Keep update execution on WebSocket/control-plane and CLI paths, and ask fleet tools to use those or an operator-side wrapper instead.

recommendation.title: Extend existing admin HTTP RPC after review
recommendation.body: Expose `update.run` through the existing disabled-by-default `admin-http-rpc` plugin only after maintainers approve the method, params, docs, private-ingress guidance, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced admin-http-rpc and have recent Gateway probe/version ownership, making them the best routing candidate for the HTTP control-plane boundary decision.
